subject: Sprint Capacity + pricing structure for mid-contract uplift & co-term alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, attached is a short proposal that covers two paths for the mid-contract uplift you described: (A) Sprint topup (short-term capacity burst) priced as a fixed monthly topup for the remainder of your term, and (B) Annualize now (move to higher committed tier with co-term alignment to 2029-03-31).

Quick summary (see attached PDF for line items):
- Sprint topup: 3 GPU pods (burst) for 3 months at a blended uplift rate (15% discount vs on-demand).
- Annualize now: convert uplift to committed capacity with a 12% incremental discount and credit for unused months pro-rated to co-term.
- Legal: we can offer a simplified amendment + order form (attached) to avoid a full SOW.

Questions I want answered before we lock pricing:
1) Do you need co-term to match your fiscal year (3/31) or calendar quarter?
2) Is there an internal procurement cap on incremental spend this quarter?
3) Any SOC2/audit constraints required for the amendment?

If it helps, I can pencil in both options and we can route the cheaper path through procurement first and legal second. Looping Karthik on pricing details and Jordan for legal cadence.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Uplift_Proposal_v1.pdf, OrderForm_BS-001.docx

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement - BrightSpring <procurement@brightspring.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Marissa — appreciate the clear options. A few quick items from procurement side:
- We prefer co-term to our fiscal year (2029-03-31).
- Current quarter incremental cap: $120k without exec approval; anything above needs finance signoff.
- We need the amendment to include a short data protection addendum (SOC2 in place already, but add explicit log retention language).

Can you confirm the expected monthly run-rate for option A (Sprint topup) vs option B (Annualize now) after credits? Also: what is the earliest effective date for a co-term conversion?

Alex
Director, Cloud Platform Procurement
BrightSpring
procurement@brightspring.com | +1 (617) 555-3300

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Alex / Marissa — looping in the pricing math. Below are the net run-rates (post-credit) based on the current contract end 2028-09-30 and co-term target 2029-03-31. Numbers intentionally conservative.

Option A - Sprint topup (3 months):
- Monthly uplift charge (Jun->Aug) = $42,000/month (fixed); no long-term commitment.
- Total 3-month spend = $126,000 (falls within your current quarter cap if booked across two billing months; otherwise needs exec signoff).

Option B - Annualize & co-term:
- Effective if signed by 2028-07-15, we credit remaining months from current term and annualize new committed units; net monthly run-rate = $34,500/month, measured post-credit.
- One-time true-up credit applied on first invoice (est. $18k).
- Requires a standard Amendment + Order Form.

Tradeoffs: Option A is faster but higher near-term spend; Option B reduces unit cost and simplifies operations into a single committed tier. Given your procurement cap, a split approach is possible: start Sprint topup immediately (Option A) and submit the Amendment for Option B with an effective date aligned to 7/1 so the true-up credit reduces next invoice. That keeps service up while you complete approvals.

Marissa — can you confirm the internal procurement milestone timing? Alex — if you share the finance approver, we can set a target approval window.

Thanks,
Karthik
Pricing Manager | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@brightspring.com <procurement@brightspring.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Karthik — thanks for the clarity. Procurement will approve a Sprint topup (Option A) if we can stagger invoicing across two billing cycles to stay under the $120k cap. If Redwood can issue two invoices (one for Jun-Jul, second for Aug) we can process without exec signoff.

On Option B, finance will review the Amendment but needs the true-up detail in dollar terms on the order form (line by line). Can you produce an updated order form with the true-up calculation and an explicit audit/log retention clause for 12 months? Sample language attached in a follow-up doc.

Procurement Team
BrightSpring

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@brightspring.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T09:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Understood — we can split the sprint invoice across two billing cycles. I'll update the order form to show the pro-rated true-up in dollar terms and add the 12-month log retention clause you requested. Jordan, can legal confirm the amendment language is acceptable for a short data protection addendum?

Proposed next steps:
- Today: Karthik will update order form + true-up calc.
- Tomorrow: I will send revised OrderForm_BS-001.docx with audit language and split invoice note.
- Early next week: Alex / Procurement to sign off and finance to do the two-invoice processing.

If procurement is comfortable, we can put the sprint topup into effect 7/1 and have the Amendment effective 7/15 to capture Option B pricing.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightspring.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightspring.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: capacity sprint pricing + co-term options

Procurement / Marissa — quick legal note: the short data protection addendum draft is fine but we need two tiny clarifications before signature: (1) define "log retention" by retention period and owner (we'll add: BrightSpring-owned logs retained 12 months, Redwoods stores for 180 days for operational diagnostics), and (2) add simple right-to-audit language limited to SOC2 evidence and redacted exports only. Neither should delay the Amendment.

Marissa — once Karthik posts the numeric true-up on the order form, I can attach the addendum and route the two-party signature via DocuSign.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Onward: Marissa to send updated docs (OrderForm_BS-001.docx) and I'll produce the addendum for signature.
